Qawmi Madrasas: Some Observations, Reflections, and Expectations

1. My Personal Connection with Qawmi Madrasas

I am not myself a graduate of a Qawmi madrasa. Nevertheless, I have always tried to maintain a positive attitude towards the Qawmi educational tradition. Many of my relatives are associated with this system, and among my students, too, there are many who studied at Qawmi madrasas. Several of my own teachers were graduates of Darul Uloom Deoband. Moreover, I once had the opportunity, on a limited scale and for a certain period, to teach an advanced course for a select group of students who had graduated from Qawmi madrasas.

My interest in the Qawmi educational system, therefore, is not merely theoretical; it is closely connected with personal relationships, teaching, and practical experience. In light of these experiences, I would like to share some of my observations and reflections on Qawmi madrasas.

## 2. The Contribution of Qawmi Madrasas to Islamic Education and Values

The contribution of Qawmi madrasas to the preservation, dissemination, and promotion of Islamic values in Bangladesh is extremely important. They have long played a significant role, particularly at the grassroots level, in expanding religious education, cultivating the recitation of the Qur’an, encouraging adherence to religious obligations, and nurturing an Islamic outlook on life. Through their close links with mosques, maktabs, madrasas, and local religious communities, these institutions have become an important foundation for religious education and practice among ordinary people.

In particular, Qawmi madrasas and associated institutions provide opportunities for Islamic education in many remote and disadvantaged areas of the country where alternative institutional facilities are limited.

Therefore, when evaluating the contribution of Qawmi madrasas, due importance must be given not only to their formal educational activities but also to their role in fostering religious consciousness, moral values, and Islamic practices at the grassroots level.

## 3. Preserving the Qawmi Tradition and Its Educational Capacity

In the present context, there is considerable scope for questioning the curriculum, educational standards, institutional management, and capacity of the Alia educational system to produce scholars with a profound knowledge of Islam.

Considering the current structure and practical realities of this system, it is difficult to expect it to produce, on a broad scale, scholars possessing deep knowledge and well-established expertise in the traditional Islamic sciences. (Of course, a limited number of qualified scholars may emerge through exceptional individual initiatives or the dedicated efforts of particular institutions.)

Under these circumstances, preserving the existence, distinctive identity, and educational capacity of Qawmi madrasas is essential for safeguarding the tradition of Islamic scholarship on a broad scale and producing qualified personnel in the Qur’an, Hadith, Fiqh, and other Islamic disciplines.

However, merely keeping these institutions in existence is not enough. Continuous improvement of the educational system must also be ensured by raising academic standards, developing awareness of contemporary knowledge and realities, and taking students’ future prospects into account.

## 4. Qawmi Madrasas in the Ideological Landscape of Bangladesh

In Bangladesh’s religious and ideological landscape, Qawmi madrasas are significant representatives of traditional Islamic scholarship, religious observance, and a distinctive outlook on life.

For this reason, there is a pronounced ideological conflict between this educational tradition and secular and liberal forces. These forces tend to view Jamaat-e-Islami more as a political rival than as an ideological adversary. On questions of religious and social values—particularly the observance of Islamic principles at the grassroots level—they regard Qawmi madrasas as a primary ideological opponent.

It is therefore reasonable to suspect that various forms of machination against Qawmi madrasas, which have occurred in the past, continue today through different strategies. Nor is there sufficient reason to assume that such activities will cease entirely in the foreseeable future.

In this context, emotional or purely reactive responses are inadequate. Rather, preparations to address potential challenges should include strengthening institutional capacity, increasing legal awareness, ensuring transparency and accountability in institutional activities, expanding public engagement, and developing effective communication and cooperation with responsible individuals who uphold Islamic values.

## 5. The Expansion of Qawmi Educational Institutions at the Grassroots Level

At present, various types of educational institutions are emerging in different parts of the country, particularly in urban neighbourhoods, residential areas, and narrow lanes, through the initiatives of Qawmi madrasa graduates and students. These include Nurani madrasas, Hifz institutions, women’s madrasas, women’s Hifz institutions, and establishments adopting modern management practices and kindergarten-style teaching methods. In some areas, multiple institutions operate within the same neighbourhood or even along the same city street. This trend represents a significant aspect of the grassroots expansion of the Qawmi educational tradition.

This expansion has at least two important positive dimensions.

First, individuals educated in the Qawmi system are establishing institutions through their own initiatives, thereby creating opportunities for employment and self-employment. Second, these institutions are bringing opportunities for Qur’anic education, basic Islamic knowledge, religious practice, and moral instruction closer to ordinary people.

At the same time, many parents are dissatisfied with the quality of teaching, management, and attention given to students in conventional educational institutions, including government primary schools. Alongside these concerns, many families also wish to ensure that their children receive Qur’anic and basic religious education. These factors have encouraged growing interest in such institutions.

Consequently, the expansion of these establishments is driven not only by religious devotion but also by parental expectations, perceptions of educational quality, and the accessibility of institutions.

However, to translate this expansion into positive long-term outcomes, it is essential to ensure educational quality, teacher training, child safety, appropriate curricula, and institutional accountability.

The principal consideration for future development should not simply be an increase in the number of institutions, but the provision of quality education, responsible management, a safe and child-friendly environment, and the all-round development of students.

## 6. The Responsibilities of Qawmi Leadership in Addressing Future Challenges

The role of senior ʿulamāʾ, respected mentors, and policymakers is extremely important in addressing the present and future challenges facing Qawmi madrasas.

Nevertheless, in my observation, there is little visible evidence of a coordinated, far-sighted, and long-term strategy on their part to address the multifaceted challenges and alleged machinations confronting this educational tradition. It is difficult to say with certainty how aware they are of potential adverse developments directed against the Qawmi educational system, whether at the national or international level, or whether they are adequately informed about the possibility of new forms of adversity. However, the apparent lack of preparedness and effective initiatives to address such challenges is a significant cause for concern.

In many instances, it seems that they are more preoccupied with their respective interests, spheres of influence, and internal affairs than with the collective interests of the broader educational tradition.

Yet coordinated initiatives are urgently needed to protect the distinctive identity and institutional existence of the Qawmi educational system; address potential adversities; maintain educational quality and improve the learning environment; create dignified employment opportunities for graduates; and enhance the social standing and professional recognition of the ʿulamāʾ.

In this regard, it is not enough to worry about the possibility of external pressure or to undertake isolated initiatives. Equally important are identifying internal weaknesses, implementing necessary reforms, and developing realistic action plans for future generations.

The Qawmi leadership needs to strengthen its efforts to formulate clear plans, ensure effective coordination, and undertake visible, practical initiatives in these areas.

## 7. Institutional Coordination, Quality Control, and Accountability

Although countless Qawmi educational institutions of various sizes have been established across the country, the effectiveness of coordination, quality control, and accountability mechanisms among them deserves careful examination. Despite the activities of various boards and regional organisations, a clearer understanding is needed of how effectively minimum educational standards, administrative transparency, and meaningful oversight are ensured across all types of institutions.

Where effective supervision and accountability are lacking, some institutions may face risks of irregularities, financial mismanagement, neglect of students’ welfare, or other unethical practices. Such problems can also be difficult to identify and remedy in institutions operating in isolation. At the same time, a lack of institutional transparency and reliable information may create opportunities for negative publicity or unfounded allegations against the educational tradition as a whole.

In these circumstances, effective mechanisms for coordination and oversight need to be developed while preserving the necessary institutional autonomy and scope for local initiative.

Such mechanisms could encompass institutional registration and identification, minimum educational standards, teacher recruitment and training, financial transparency, student safety, the learning environment, complaint resolution, and regular evaluation. In addition, a credible framework is essential for the impartial investigation and resolution of allegations of misconduct.

Such arrangements are not intended to undermine the distinctive identity of Qawmi madrasas. Rather, they are necessary to strengthen their institutional foundations, protect students’ rights, and enhance public trust and social acceptance.
